Define, for non-negative integers \(n\),

\[S_{n}:=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{k^{n}}{k!}\]

where \(0^{0}=1\) when it occurs. Then \(S_{0}=e\), and, for \(n \geq 1\),

\[S_{n}=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{k^{n}}{k!}=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{k^{n}}{k!}=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{(k+1)^{n}}{(k+1)!}=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{(k+1)^{n-1}}{k!}=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\binom{n-1}{i} S_{i},\]

so we can compute inductively that \(S_{1}=e, S_{2}=2 e, S_{3}=5 e\), and \(S_{4}=15 e\).
